title: The Dhamaal Boys Are Back. This Time, There's a Mountain of Gold and Absolutely Zero Common Sense.
excerpt: Dhamaal 4 hits theatres July 10 with Ajay Devgn, Arshad Warsi, and the entire original gang — and it moved its release date to dodge Christopher Nolan.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Dhamaal 4 releases on July 10, 2026, featuring the original cast and new additions.
  • The film's plot revolves around a chaotic treasure hunt with comedic twists.
  • Trade analysts predict an opening day collection of ₹13-15 crore for Dhamaal 4.
  • The release date was moved to avoid competition with Christopher Nolan's *The Odyssey*.
  • The franchise remains popular among diaspora audiences for its family-friendly humor.
The Gang's Return
›Original cast: Ajay Devgn, Arshad Warsi, Riteish Deshmukh, Jaaved Jaaferi.
›New cast includes Esha Gupta and Ravi Kishan.
›Ravi Kishan claims it's a 'very well-written film'.
›Sanjay Mishra returns as the emotional anchor.

The last time the Dhamaal franchise showed up in theatres, *Total Dhamaal* (2019) collected over ₹150 crore and reminded everyone that there's no substitute for watching four grown men lose their minds over buried treasure. Seven years later, the gang is back — louder, dumber, and more expensive than ever.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=IG-eByZdz6Y

*Dhamaal 4* arrives on July 10, 2026, and if the trailer is any indication, director Indra Kumar has learned exactly one lesson from the previous three films: more chaos, always more chaos.

The Gang's All Here

![Christopher Nolan — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/49/ChrisNolanBFI150224_%2810_of_12%29_%2853532289710%29_%28cropped2%29.jpg)

The core four return: Ajay Devgn, Arshad Warsi, Riteish Deshmukh, and Jaaved Jaaferi — the quartet whose combined screen energy oscillates between genius and clinical insanity. Sanjay Mishra, who joined the franchise in *Total Dhamaal* and immediately became its emotional anchor (which says everything about this franchise), is back as well.

New additions include Esha Gupta, Sanjeeda Shaikh, Anjali Anand, Ravi Kishan, Upendra Limaye, and Vijay Patkar. Ravi Kishan, who plays a pirate in the film, has been making the rounds calling it "a very well-written film" that will "revive Bollywood comedy." Bold claim from a man dressed as a pirate, but in the Dhamaal universe, stranger things have been true.

> "That target isn't unreasonable — it needs to beat Cocktail 2's ₹14.1 crore opening to crack the top four, and the franchise has the brand recognition to do it."

> "Yeh comedy daur hain aur ismein Dhamaal bahut chalegi because it's a very well-written film. Uske sab jokes land karenge." — Ravi Kishan

The Plot (Such As It Is)

The trailer, which launched with a spectacularly bonkers event at Imagicaa amusement park — complete with a 60-foot poster unfurled at the park's grand waterfall — reveals the outline: the Dhamaal boys set off on the biggest treasure hunt of their lives. A mountain of gold awaits. So does a mountain of trouble.

Who gets to the treasure first? Who betrays whom? Who falls off a cliff for comedy? All of these questions will be answered, probably in the first twenty minutes, before the film pivots to an entirely new set of catastrophes. That's the Dhamaal formula, and nobody's messing with it.

![Arshad Warsi — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/9e/Arshad-Warsi.jpg)

The film is presented by Gulshan Kumar and T-Series, produced by Bhushan Kumar, Ajay Devgn, Kumar Mangat Pathak, and Indra Kumar himself under Devgn Films, Maruti International, and Panorama Studios.

Dodging Nolan

Here's a fun detail: Dhamaal 4 was originally scheduled for July 17. Then the makers looked at the calendar and saw Christopher Nolan's *The Odyssey* sitting right there — a film that will devour every IMAX screen and premium format slot in the country. Rather than go head-to-head with Nolan (a fight nobody wins), the team moved their release a week earlier to July 10, giving the film a clean solo window.

Smart move. Nolan remains one of the most bankable filmmakers in India — *Oppenheimer* was a cultural event, *Interstellar* still plays in IMAX re-releases — and *The Odyssey* advance booking has already begun with a "super solid" response. Dhamaal 4 needs its own runway, and now it has one.

Box Office Expectations

![Riteish Deshmukh — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/eb/Riteish_Deshmukh_at_the_Promotion_of_%27Kyaa_Super_Kool_Hain_Hum%27_06.jpg)

Trade analysts are predicting a ₹13-15 crore opening day, which would put it in the top five Bollywood openers of 2026. That target isn't unreasonable — it needs to beat Cocktail 2's ₹14.1 crore opening to crack the top four, and the franchise has the brand recognition to do it.

The timing also works in its favour. Alpha opened to a lukewarm ₹9.25 crore and is facing mixed-to-negative word of mouth. Baby Do Die Do barely registered. Welcome To The Jungle is into its second week and losing screens. The theatrical landscape on July 10 is essentially an open goal for a family entertainer that delivers.

Why Diaspora Audiences Should Care

The Dhamaal franchise has always been comfort food for the Indian diaspora — the kind of movie you watch with family on a Sunday afternoon, where nobody needs subtitles for the humour and everyone laughs at the same beats. For NRIs in North America and the UK, these films show up reliably in multiplexes, and they're one of the few Bollywood franchises where you can take your parents and your kids without anyone cringing.

Strategic Release Timing
›Originally scheduled for July 17, moved to July 10.
›Avoids competition with Nolan's *The Odyssey*.
›July 10 offers a clean solo window for family audiences.

With the July 4th long weekend wrapping up and the summer school break in full swing, Dhamaal 4's July 10 release is perfectly positioned for diaspora family outings. It's not art. It's not trying to be. It's four idiots chasing gold, and sometimes that's exactly what you need.

Expect this one to have legs.
